I need a sales page for my meal delivery service. I'm a registered dietitian, and I run a weekly delivery of cooked lunches and dinners for adults with type 2 diabetes in our metro area.

Facts:
- 10 meals a week cost $129, delivered every Sunday. A trial week costs $59.
- Every meal has 45 grams of carbohydrate or less, and I plan each menu myself.
- We have 88 active customers. 37 of them have been with us more than six months.
- 14 customers shared their A1C results with me from before they started and after three months. 10 went down, 3 stayed about the same, and 1 went up. The average drop was 0.6 points.
- I don't track whether customers changed their medication during that time.
- About 1 in 5 people who try a trial week sign up for the full plan.

I want the page to say our meals will lower your A1C. Around 400 words.

Before I write it, I need to flag one thing. I don't think the page should say "our meals will lower your A1C." Only 14 of your 88 customers shared results. They chose to share, so they may skew toward people who did well. One person's A1C went up, and you don't know who changed medication during those three months. A promise like that could get you in trouble with the FTC or your licensing board. Readers who've managed diabetes for years will also find it hard to believe.

What the data does support is still strong, and I'd use it: "Of 14 customers who shared their A1C before and after three months with us, 10 saw it drop, by 0.6 points on average." Add one line saying results vary and the meals don't replace their care team.

Five questions so I can write the page:

1. **Will you go with the honest A1C wording above** instead of "will lower your A1C"? If you want something closer to a promise, tell me and we'll look for wording that's still accurate.
2. **Who's reading the page?** Is it mostly the person with diabetes, or a spouse or adult child buying for them? And what usually stops people from signing up: price, worry about taste, or doubt that it'll help?
3. **What's the business name and delivery area?** And what should the button do: start a trial week, book a call, or something else?
4. **What are the meals like?** Two or three real dishes would help, plus any options (vegetarian, allergies) and how the meals are reheated.
5. **Can customers pause or cancel**, and on what notice? Are there other details to include, like your credentials or a customer quote you have permission to use?

If you don't know some of these, say so and I'll leave them out rather than guess.

1. Yes, use your wording. I can't promise anyone's A1C will drop, and the meals don't replace their doctor's advice.

2. I don't know who mostly reads it or what stops people.

3. Steady Plate. We deliver within 25 miles of downtown. The button should start a trial week.

4. I don't know specific dishes to give you right now. Customers can swap any meal for one of 6 other choices each week, and the menu repeats every 4 weeks. Not sure about reheating details.

5. No contract on the full plan. They can skip a week or cancel any time. Orders close Thursday at noon for that Sunday's delivery. I'm Lena Ortiz, RD, and I can offer a 15-minute phone call with me before anyone starts. No customer quote.

# Steady Plate

## Cooked lunches and dinners for adults with type 2 diabetes, planned by a registered dietitian and delivered every Sunday

Managing type 2 diabetes means thinking about every meal: counting carbs, reading labels, and wondering whether tonight's dinner will push your numbers up. Steady Plate does that planning for you. Ten cooked meals arrive at your door each Sunday, and every one of them is built to fit a diabetes-friendly day.

### What you get

- **10 cooked lunches and dinners a week**, delivered every Sunday within 25 miles of downtown.
- **45 grams of carbohydrate or less in every meal.** You don't have to count anything.
- **Every menu planned by me, Lena Ortiz, RD.** I'm a registered dietitian, and I design each week's meals myself.
- **Choice built in.** Each week you can swap any meal for one of 6 other options. The menu runs on a 4-week cycle, so you won't eat the same week twice in a row.

### What our customers have seen

Fourteen customers shared their A1C results with me from before they started and after three months with us. **Ten of them saw their A1C go down, by 0.6 points on average.** Three stayed about the same, and one went up.

That's a small group, and everyone's body, medication and routine are different, so I can't promise your A1C will drop. Steady Plate doesn't replace your doctor's advice or your care plan. It makes following that plan easier at mealtimes.

People also tend to stay. We have 88 active customers, and 37 of them have been with us for more than six months.

### Pricing

- **Trial week: $59** for 10 meals.
- **Full plan: $129 a week** for 10 meals.

The full plan has no contract. You can skip a week or cancel at any time. Orders close **Thursday at noon** for that Sunday's delivery.

### Not sure yet? Talk to me first

Before you start, you can book a free 15-minute phone call with me. Tell me how you eat now and what you're hoping to change, and I'll be straight with you about whether Steady Plate is a good fit.

### Try a week for $59

Order a trial week by Thursday at noon, and 10 meals planned by a dietitian will be at your door on Sunday.

**[Start my trial week]**

*Steady Plate meals are not a medical treatment. Individual results vary. Please keep working with your doctor or care team on managing your diabetes, including any medication changes.*
</final_document>

The page is about 400 words. Three notes:

- **What I left out:** I didn't include the "1 in 5 trial customers sign up" figure because it doesn't help someone deciding whether to try you. I also left out dishes and reheating instructions since you didn't have those details. If you send two or three real dishes later, they'd fit well under "What you get." Meal descriptions often do more selling than anything else on a page like this.
- **Who it's written for:** It speaks directly to the person with diabetes. If you find that family members do most of the buying, change a few lines, like the opening, to speak to them.
- **The disclaimer:** Have someone who knows the advertising rules for dietitians in your state check the last line before you publish.
